scenarios.name: Landing Page Hero Section Validation
scenarios.description: Validates that the hero section clearly communicates what MirDB is and includes a compelling tagline and primary CTA

steps.description: User opens the website homepage
steps.context: Initial user entry point

steps.description: User sees project name, tagline, and description at the top of the page
steps.context: User needs to understand project purpose within first impression

steps.description: User can see and access primary call-to-action buttons for GitHub and getting started
steps.context: Critical navigation for conversion funnel

test_cases.expected: Hero section displays clear tagline explaining MirDB as a persistent memcached-compatible key-value store
Project description is concise and understandable to target audience
Link opens GitHub repository in new tab
User is navigated to getting started section or page
Hero section content scales properly, text remains readable, buttons are accessible

scenarios.name: Features Section Content Validation
scenarios.description: Validates that all key features are presented accurately with icons and descriptions

steps.description: User scrolls or navigates to the features section
steps.context: After understanding project purpose, user wants to evaluate capabilities

steps.description: User examines the memcached protocol compatibility feature card
steps.context: Critical feature for drop-in replacement usage

steps.description: User examines the SSTable-based persistence feature
steps.context: Key differentiator from traditional memcached

steps.description: User examines the LSM tree architecture feature
steps.context: Technical depth important for database audience

steps.description: User examines the Tokio async runtime feature
steps.context: Performance credibility for modern applications

test_cases.expected: All key features (Memcached Protocol, Persistence, LSM Tree, Async Performance) are displayed with clear descriptions
Each feature has accurate, concise description matching PRD requirements
Each feature includes an icon or visual element that enhances understanding
Memcached compatibility includes correct command list (SET, GET, DELETE, etc.)
Feature cards stack vertically and remain readable

scenarios.name: Architecture Diagram and Documentation
scenarios.description: Validates that architecture section explains data flow and technical implementation clearly

steps.description: User scrolls or navigates to the architecture overview section
steps.context: Technical users want to understand implementation details

steps.description: User examines the architecture diagram showing data flow
steps.context: Visual representation aids understanding

steps.description: User reads write path explanation (WAL → Memtable → SSTable)
steps.context: Understanding insert/update operations

steps.description: User reads read path explanation (key lookup process)
steps.context: Understanding query operations

steps.description: User reads compaction process documentation
steps.context: Understanding space optimization and performance

test_cases.expected: Visual diagram clearly illustrates data flow between WAL, Memtable, and SSTable components

test_cases.input: Verify diagrams are exported as static assets
test_cases.expected: SVG or other vector format images are properly exported with HTML

scenarios.name: Getting Started Section Validation

test_cases.expected: Standard memcached commands list includes: SET, GET, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND
Custom commands include: INFO, MAJOR_COMPACTION
Each command has syntax, parameters, and return values documented
